lines.text: Here's how to pick the right Claude model, in under sixty seconds.
Four, from small to big: Haiku, Sonnet, Opus and Fable. Smaller is cheaper and faster; bigger handles harder work.
Say your app has four jobs: tagging ten thousand tickets, a chat reply a customer waits on, a tricky bug, and a big migration.
Rule one: start on Opus, the daily driver, at medium effort. Effort is how long it thinks first. The tricky bug stays here.
Rule two: move down for simple jobs, or when someone's waiting. Tagging goes to Haiku, at a fortieth of the price. The chat reply goes to Sonnet: it's fast.
Rule three: if it falls short, don't jump yet. Give it a way to check its work, like a test, then raise the effort. Only then move up: the migration goes to Fable.
And compare cost per task, not price per token: on one coding test, Fable matched Opus at max effort, for about half the cost.
